aesthetic: The Living-Room Handoff — a CTV ad-ops console
anchor: The demand-side-platform (DSP) campaign console crossed with the warm glow of a living-room screen at night: an instrument panel reading a household 'match' against a streaming slate, where a cool-blue mobile signal is handed across a lossy identity bridge to a warm-amber television. Descends from the two-screen handoff (phone glass → TV glass), the dotted identity-graph match line, and the ad-ops readout of match rates and deal IDs in monospace.
rationale: The corpus's structural metaphor is the handoff: an individual first-party signal captured on a phone, resolved through a clean room, and served to a household on the biggest screen in the house — most of the value leaking to toll-keepers in between. So the palette is deliberately two-tone: a cool electric blue for the mobile/programmatic signal (t2) and a warm amber 'screen glow' for the living-room television (accent, t1), with violet for the identity-bridge match (t3), teal for the margin/money (t4), and coral for leakage/loss/refutation (t5). The dark mode is native — a dark living room lit by a screen; the technical-grotesque display font and monospace data strings evoke the ad-ops console, not an essay.
